title: Min Stack
statement: Build a stack that supports push, pop, top and getMin. The first three work as usual. getMin returns the smallest value currently in the stack. Every method must run in constant time.

example.caption: After pushing -2, 0, -3 the minimum is -3. Pop removes -3, and the minimum goes back to -2.

idea.sentence: Keep a second stack that stores the smallest value at every level, so popping simply reveals the older minimum.

jargon.plain: A pile where you only add or remove at the top: last in, first out.
Constant time. The cost does not grow with the number of items.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: method names, then their arguments. e.g. ["MinStack","push","getMin"] and [[],[4],[]]

vars.meaning: number of values in the stack

compare.optimalLabel: getMin reads the top of the min stack

rows.name: Scan on getMin
rows.note: Push, pop and top are O(1), but finding the smallest means looking at every value.

rows.name: Two stacks
rows.note: The second stack is exactly as tall as the first. The price is one extra number per value.

fast.takeaway: Store the answer to getMin at every level when you push. Then pop undoes it for free, with no search.

stages.title: Two stacks
stages.note: vals holds the values. mins holds, at each level, the smallest value at or below that level.

stages.title: Push both
stages.note: Push the value. Push the smaller of the value and the current minimum on the min stack.

stages.title: Pop both
stages.note: Remove the top of each stack. The older minimum is now on top of the min stack.

stages.title: Top
stages.note: Read the last value of the normal stack.

stages.title: Get min
stages.note: Read the last value of the min stack. Nothing to search.

edges.title: One value
edges.why: The first value is its own minimum. The stack is empty, so there is nothing to compare with.

edges.title: Same minimum twice
edges.why: Each push gets its own min entry. If only strictly smaller values were stored, this pop would erase the last 1.

edges.title: Pop to the older min
edges.why: The min stack remembers what the minimum was before -1 arrived.

edges.title: Extreme values
edges.why: Only comparisons are used, no subtraction, so there is no overflow.

gotchas.text: A single min variable is not enough. After popping the minimum you would have to rescan the stack to find the next one.
Push to the min stack on every push, not only when the value is smaller. Otherwise duplicates of the minimum break on pop.
Math.min(...stack) works, but it scans the whole array on each call and can overflow the call stack for very large arrays. It is the slow solution in disguise.
Use a pointer receiver on Push and Pop. With a value receiver the method changes a copy and the stack never grows.
s.vals[len(s.vals)-1] panics on an empty slice. The problem promises top and getMin are only called on a non-empty stack, so a check is optional here, but real code needs one.

recap.key: Every push also records the smallest value so far. Every pop removes both. getMin reads the top of the second stack.
recap.complexity: Time O(1) per call. Space O(n).
moves: Keep vals and mins, always the same height
On push, add min(value, current min) to mins
getMin returns the top of mins
